GO-ORA Network Analysis Workflow

network-analysis.Rmd

Introduction

This vignette walks through the scoranet workflow: cluster-specific differential expression, GO over-representation analysis (GO-ORA), pathway overlap networks, and interpretation of the network modules.

The workflow:

  1. Differential expression (DE) within each cell-type cluster
  2. GO over-representation analysis on each cluster’s DEGs
  3. Pathway overlap networks with Leiden clustering
  4. Diagnostics to choose the network settings
  5. Interpreting modules: cluster themes, driver genes, and word clouds

Load Packages 

library(scoranet)
library(org.Mm.eg.db)

Input Data

This workflow assumes a normalized Seurat object named seurat_obj with a metadata column of cell-type clusters (final_celltype) and one of samples (sample). This example compares Car against Bleo within two fibroblast clusters. Seurat 4 and Seurat 5 objects both work; Seurat 5 layers split by sample are joined automatically.

1. Differential Expression 

de_results <- run_cluster_de(
  obj         = seurat_obj,
  clusters    = c("Fibroblast 1", "Fibroblast 2"),
  cluster_col = "final_celltype",
  ident_col   = "sample",
  ident1      = "Car",
  ident2      = "Bleo"
)

Each cluster’s result is a list with two data frames:

  • degs: genes passing padj_thresh (default 0.05) and logfc_thresh (default 0.5), with a res column giving the direction.
  • tested: every gene FindMarkers tested.

Which genes get tested is controlled by two FindMarkers pre-filters, seurat_min_pct (default 0.1) and seurat_logfc_threshold (default 0.25). They are set explicitly because the FindMarkers defaults differ between Seurat 4 and 5. A short summary (tested genes, DEGs, and DEGs up in each identity) is printed for each cluster.

Write the results to disk: <cluster>_DE_Results.csv (DEGs) and <cluster>_tested_genes.csv (all tested genes).

write_de(de_results, outSubDir = "results/DE/")

2. GO Over-Representation Analysis 

go_results <- run_go_ora(
  de_list   = de_results,
  org_db    = org.Mm.eg.db,
  universe  = rownames(seurat_obj),
  ont       = "BP",
  outputDir = "results/GO/"
)

write_go(go_results, outSubDir = "results/GO/")

Useful options:

  • use_tested_universe = TRUE: use each cluster’s tested genes as the background instead of universe. This is usually the more accurate background, because genes that were never tested could not have been DEGs.
  • split_direction = TRUE: run ORA separately on up- and down-regulated DEGs. Pass the same setting to write_go() and run_comparison_networks(); a mismatch is an error.
  • simplify = TRUE: remove redundant GO terms with clusterProfiler::simplify(). Off by default, because the networks below already group redundant terms.

A QC summary of tested and retained gene sets per cluster is written to outputDir.

3. Pathway Overlap Networks 

net_results <- run_comparison_networks(
  go_list           = go_results,
  de_list           = de_results,
  comp_label        = "Car_vs_Bleo",
  base_outdir       = "results/",
  overlap_threshold = 0.1,
  leiden_resolution = 1
)

Nodes are enriched GO terms. Two terms are connected when the Jaccard overlap of their DE genes is at least overlap_threshold; terms with no connection are dropped. Terms are then grouped with Leiden clustering (modularity objective, seeded so results are reproducible).

Each term’s direction is called from a z-score of its DE genes ((n_up - n_down) / sqrt(n_up + n_down)): up, down, or mixed, with zscore_threshold (default 1) as the cutoff. Mean and median log2 fold changes are kept alongside.

Each element of net_results holds the igraph network, a go_term_df table of terms and clusters, and four editable ggplot objects in $plots, also saved to results/Car_vs_Bleo/networks/:

Plot Shows
plain Nodes coloured by direction (up, down, mixed)
leiden Nodes coloured by Leiden cluster
zscore Nodes coloured by a continuous direction z-score
themes Each cluster outlined and labelled with its shared GO parent terms 
net_results[["Fibroblast 1"]]$plots$themes

The themes plot labels each cluster with up to two higher-level GO terms that its terms fall under, with how many terms they cover (for example “cell cycle (48/59)”). A cluster with no specific shared parent is labelled with its most connected term and flagged; this usually means the cluster mixes unrelated terms. Use theme_label = "keywords", "phrase", or "hub" for other label styles. The labels are also available as a table:

net_results[["Fibroblast 1"]]$cluster_themes

4. Choosing Network Settings with Diagnostics

run_network_diagnostics() builds four diagnostic figures, all returned as editable ggplot objects and optionally saved as PNGs:

dx <- run_network_diagnostics(
  net_list = net_results,
  de_list  = de_results,
  go_list  = go_results,
  outdir   = "results/Car_vs_Bleo/diagnostics/"
)

dx$overview                                       # DEGs, terms, clusters per cell type
dx$networks[["Fibroblast 1"]]$overlap_threshold   # terms kept and dropped by threshold
dx$networks[["Fibroblast 1"]]$leiden_sweep        # clusters, modularity, stability by resolution
dx$networks[["Fibroblast 1"]]$driver_genes        # genes each cluster is built on

Each function can also be run on its own: plot_comparison_overview(), plot_overlap_threshold(), plot_leiden_sweep(), and plot_driver_genes().

Suggested order:

  1. Overlap threshold. Choose the threshold that cuts most weak edges while dropping few terms. With small GO terms, a threshold of 0.1 can let a single shared gene connect two terms; 0.2 is often a better starting point.
  2. Leiden resolution. After setting the threshold, choose a resolution on a plateau where the cluster count is steady, modularity is high, and stability is close to 1.
  3. Re-run run_comparison_networks() with the chosen overlap_threshold and leiden_resolution.

DIAGNOSTICS.md in the package repository explains how to read each figure.

5. Interpreting Modules

Word clouds

Word clouds of each cluster’s GO term names:

write_cluster_wordclouds_patchwork(
  net_list   = net_results,
  outputDir  = "results/",
  comparison = "Car_vs_Bleo"
)

Cluster membership

Export every GO term with its Leiden cluster and direction statistics:

for (nm in names(net_results)) {
  write.csv(
    net_results[[nm]]$go_term_df,
    file = file.path("results/Car_vs_Bleo/networks",
                     paste0(gsub("[ /]", "_", nm), "_cluster_membership.csv")),
    row.names = FALSE
  )
}

Terms in one module

Extract all GO terms in the same Leiden cluster as a term of interest, for example the extracellular matrix module:

ecm_terms <- write_cluster_results(
  net_result = net_results[["Fibroblast 1"]],
  go_term    = "extracellular matrix organization",
  outdir     = "results/Car_vs_Bleo/networks/"
)
